text:
Mark Stone became the Golden Knights' career points leader on Nov. 20, setting up Victor Olofsson for his 418th point with the franchise, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger noted. NHL.com called him the "epitome of being a Golden Knight" before the trip to Edmonton, which is about right for the captain of the team that won the Cup in 2023.

This season's line is good: 11 goals and 23 points in 26 games, 13 of them on the power play. Our numbers are less sure about the engine. Vegas has scored 7.6 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, he's shooting 25%, and his five-on-five impact is negative relative to his teammates this year.

That's a change from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him third among all forwards in wins above replacement and strong defensively. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 96th percentile for primary shot assists.

So the record is earned over eight years. The current pace leans on luck. The question is whether his underlying play climbs back toward what it was.
headline: Mark Stone, the franchise's points leader
